name: Eagles 2026 system
summary: A charting and diagramming language for the 2026 Eagles offense, rebuilt from the two playbooks closest to Sean Mannion: Green Bay 2019 (LaFleur, where he coached in 2024 and 2025) and the Rams 2022 (McVay, the offense he played in from 2017 to 2018). When the two books use different words for the same thing, the Green Bay word is the main one and the Rams word is listed as an alias.
honesty: Nobody outside the building knows the real Eagles words. This is the family language, used the same way every week so the film charts and the drawings line up. Where film cannot show which receiver has which job, the system says so instead of guessing.

gb-2019.title: Green Bay 2019 (LaFleur)
gb-2019.note: Page = page of the PDF. Open it in the reader.

rams-2022.title: Rams 2022 (McVay)
rams-2022.note: Page = page inside that section's PDF.

lineage.system: Fisher staff, then McVay from 2017 with LaFleur as coordinator
lineage.why: The 2017 Rams language is what LaFleur carried to Green Bay, so the Green Bay 2019 book is close to what he played in.

lineage.system: Kubiak and Stefanski wide zone in Minnesota, then O'Connell (McVay tree). Waldron (McVay tree) in Seattle
lineage.why: Same family the whole way: wide zone, play pass off it, keepers.
His only coaching stop before Philadelphia. This is why the Green Bay word wins a tie.
What the weekly film chart is recording.

principles.title: Motion and shifts on most snaps
principles.means: Motion at the snap, fly motion, and shifts from empty back to a normal set, so the defense cannot key run or pass from the picture.
principles.chart: Always fill in the Motion note: who, from where, which way, moving or set at the snap.

principles.title: Under center and wide zone
principles.means: The run game starts with wide zone from under center, with mid zone, tight zone and gap runs built off the same looks.
principles.chart: Record under center, gun or pistol on every snap. It is part of the call.

principles.title: Play pass that looks like the run
principles.means: Play action and keepers are tied to a run number, so the first two steps of the line and the back look like the run.
principles.chart: Name the run the fake copies (for example Pass 18) before naming the routes.

principles.title: Pure progression reads
principles.means: The quarterback reads one, two, three in order instead of picking a side from the coverage.
principles.chart: When drawing a pass, number the progression.

callOrder.means: A call is said in a fixed order. Chart and name plays in the same order so every week reads the same.

positions.means: Tight end. The formation strength is his side: Rt and Lt in a call mean where the Y goes.
Mostly the strong-side receiver. Off the ball when a tight end is on his side.
Mostly the weak-side receiver, on the ball.
The adjuster: the formation word talks to him. Fullback in 21, second tight end in 12, third receiver in 11.

personnel.means: 1 back, 1 tight end, 3 receivers. F is the third receiver.
1 back, 2 tight ends, 2 receivers. F is the second tight end.
1 back, 3 tight ends, 1 receiver. The receiver is tagged X or Z: 13X, 13Z.
2 backs, 1 tight end, 2 receivers. F is the fullback.
2 backs, 2 tight ends, 1 receiver, tagged 22X or 22Z.
2 backs, 3 receivers. The third receiver plays the Y spot.
1 back, 4 receivers. The fourth receiver plays the Y spot.
No back. 01 = 1 tight end and 4 receivers, 02 = 2 tight ends and 3 receivers.
Jumbo: an extra lineman plays a tight end spot (Rams word).

alignment.means: Every player in a formation stands on one of the editor's snap spots, so an imported formation and one I draw by hand line up the same way. These are the rules an import follows.
rules: On the ball next to the tackle: one yard outside him, on the row spacing the editor shows in orange. The next man is one more yard out.
A -5- on a playbook diagram is the Hash +5 landmark. A -3- is Hash +3. Hash +1 to +5 are the reduced splits. A stacked or bunched partner sits one yard either side of the man on the landmark.
Receiver or tight end drawn INSIDE the numbers: Top #s (the inside edge of the paint). Well inside: #s -1 or #s -2.
Drawn OUTSIDE the numbers: Bottom #s (the outside edge of the paint).
Normal outside split with nothing marked: #s +2 (the books' 2 yards outside the numbers to the field). Into the boundary: #s +4.
Very wide: 4 from the sideline or 2 from the sideline.
Slot with no mark: halfway between the end man and the outside receiver (the editor's middle snap).
A pack pushed out to the numbers covers them: inside man Top #s, point man Mid #s on the ball, outside man Bottom #s.
If a playbook shows a spot none of these cover, add a new landmark for it instead of eyeballing it.
Depths: under center the halfback's toes are at 7.5 yards and the fullback's heels at 5. Gun: quarterback's heels at 5, back beside him. Pistol: quarterback at 4, back at 7.

backfield.means: Under center is the default. No word is said.
Quarterback in the shotgun, back beside him. Said before the formation: Gun Trips Rt.
backfield.chart: Gun, RB L or Gun, RB R

backfield.means: Quarterback at 4 yards, back straight behind him.

Neither book has a word for which side of the quarterback the gun back stands on. The play tells him. The chart still records it, so PlayForge keeps it as a note on the formation: strong = the Y's side.

families.name: 2 Back
families.means: Two backs behind the quarterback. The word says where the F (the second back) stands.

families.name: 3x1 'T'
families.means: One back. Three receivers to the Y's side counting the Y, one away. Words start with T.

families.name: Bunch 'B'
families.means: 3x1 with the three squeezed into a bunch near the tackle. Words start with B.

families.name: 2x2 'D'
families.means: One back. Y and one receiver strong, two receivers weak. Words start with D.

families.name: 2x2 Stack 'S'
families.means: 2x2 with the two weak receivers tight together at a 5 yard split. Words start with S.

families.name: 1x3 'F'
families.means: One back. The Y alone on his side, three receivers away from him. Words start with F.

families.name: 1x3 Bunch 'CR'
families.means: 1x3 with the three weak receivers in a bunch. Words start with CR.

families.name: Big
families.means: 22, 13 and 23 personnel. Same words as the 2 back and 3x1 sets, with the personnel in front.

families.name: Empty
families.means: No back behind the quarterback. Call the one-back formation the other four make, then a letter for where the back lined up.

formations.means: F straight behind the quarterback, H behind him.
formations.onFilm: Two backs stacked behind the quarterback.

formations.means: F offset to the Y's side, behind the tackle's inside leg.
formations.onFilm: Fullback cheated toward the tight end.

formations.means: F offset away from the Y.
formations.onFilm: Fullback cheated away from the tight end.

formations.means: Split backs at 5 yards, F on the Y's side. Change is the same picture with the backs swapped.
formations.onFilm: A back on each side of the quarterback. In the gun this is the two-back look.

formations.means: F off the ball just outside the Y. One back.
formations.onFilm: Two tight ends on the same side, the outside one a step off the ball (a wing).

formations.means: F off the ball just inside the Y.
formations.onFilm: A wing tucked between the tackle and the tight end.

formations.means: Y on the line, F in the slot, Z outside. X alone away.
formations.onFilm: Tight end attached with two receivers outside him, one receiver on the other side.

formations.means: Trips with the Z in the slot and the F outside.
formations.onFilm: Same picture as Trips. Only the names of the two receivers change.

formations.means: Trips with the X as the outside receiver on the strong side and the F alone away.
formations.onFilm: Same picture as Trips.

formations.means: Three detached: F inside, Y in the middle, Z outside.
formations.onFilm: No attached tight end on the three-receiver side. The tight end is the middle man.

formations.means: Three detached with the Y as the outside man: F inside on the ball at a 3 yard split, Z in the middle.
formations.onFilm: Tight end split widest on the three-receiver side.

formations.means: Y inside and off, F at the point on the ball, Z outside and off.
formations.onFilm: Three in a tight triangle just outside the tackle, tight end the inside man.

formations.means: Bunch with the Y at the point.
formations.onFilm: Tight end is the man on the ball in the middle of the bunch.

formations.means: Bunch with the Y outside.
formations.onFilm: Tight end is the outside man of the bunch.

formations.means: Bunch with the X as the outside man and the F alone away.
formations.onFilm: Same picture as Bunch.

formations.means: A tight end on the line each side, a receiver outside each.
formations.onFilm: Balanced: tight end and receiver both sides.

formations.means: Y and Z strong. X outside and F in the slot weak.
formations.onFilm: Tight end attached with one receiver, two receivers away.

formations.means: Dice with the F outside and the X in the slot.
formations.onFilm: Same picture as Dice.

formations.means: Dice with Open: the Y leaves the tackle and stands in the slot, the Z takes the ball.
formations.onFilm: 2x2 with no attached tight end. He is flexed 5 yards or more.

formations.means: Weak side: F on the ball at a 5 yard split, X off the ball on his outside hip.
formations.onFilm: Two receivers tight together a few yards outside the weak tackle.

formations.means: Stack with the jobs swapped: X on the ball, F on his outside hip.
formations.onFilm: Same picture as Stack.

formations.means: X on the ball at a 5 yard split, F off the ball inside him.
formations.onFilm: Tight weak pair with the inside man off the ball.

formations.means: Stack, South and Sink with Clamp on the strong side: Y off the ball, Z at 5 yards on the ball. Everybody is condensed.
formations.onFilm: Four receivers all within about 5 yards of the tackles.

formations.means: Y alone on his side. X, Z and F spread out away from him.
formations.onFilm: Tight end with nobody outside him, three receivers on the other side. The chart calls this 3x1 toward the receivers. The call goes the other way, to the Y.

formations.means: Fast with the three receivers' jobs moved around.
formations.onFilm: Same picture as Fast.

formations.means: Y alone on his side, three receivers bunched away from him. Crack, Crush and Cruz move the jobs inside the bunch.
formations.onFilm: Tight end one side, a three-man bunch on the other.

aliases.term: Speed Pack. Crack = Sprint Pack, Crush = Fast Pack, Cruz = Swift Pack

formations.means: 13 personnel: Y strong with the Z in the slot, the other two tight ends together on the weak side.
formations.onFilm: Two tight ends away from the receiver.

variations.means: Z cuts his split to 5 yards from the end man, off the ball.
variations.onFilm: Strong receiver tucked in near the tight end.

variations.means: Z lines up on the Y's hip, like a wing. Usually a tight end body.
variations.onFilm: A second attached body outside the tight end.

variations.means: Z at 5 yards ON the ball. The Y backs off the ball next to the tackle.
variations.onFilm: Tight end off the ball, receiver on the ball just outside him.

variations.means: Z on the ball inside. The Y takes the 5 yard split off the ball outside him.
variations.onFilm: Receiver next to the tackle, tight end outside him and off.

variations.means: Y takes a 5 yard split from the tackle.
variations.onFilm: Tight end standing up, flexed off the tackle.

variations.means: Y lines up as the outside receiver. Z comes into the slot.
variations.onFilm: Tight end split widest on his side.

variations.means: Y off the ball next to the tackle.
variations.onFilm: Tight end attached but a step back.

variations.means: X cuts his split to 5 yards from the tackle.
X in a three point stance next to the weak tackle. Usually a tight end body.
variations.onFilm: An attached body on the weak side.

variations.means: Z leaves the Y's side and lines up in the weak slot, inside the X.
variations.onFilm: Both receivers away from the tight end.

variations.means: Slot with the jobs swapped: Z outside on the weak side, X in the slot.
Z weak at a 5 yard split from the tackle, ON the ball. The inside man is on.
variations.onFilm: Two receivers weak, the inside one reduced and on the line.

variations.means: Hip with the Z OFF the ball. The outside man is on.
variations.onFilm: Two receivers weak, the inside one reduced and off the line.

variations.means: Close and Tight together: both outside receivers at 5 yards.
Both outside receivers on the numbers.
variations.onFilm: Splits pulled in to the numbers.

variations.means: Inside the numbers: 2 yards inside to the field, 1 yard inside to the boundary.
variations.onFilm: Receivers a little inside the numbers.

variations.means: Plus widens the single receiver's split, minus cuts it down.
variations.onFilm: Lone receiver wider or tighter than normal.

empty.means: In an empty set the call is the one-back formation the other four make, then a letter for the back. Letters run across the field from the strong side.

letters.means: Widest man on the strong side.
Tight to the strong side, off the ball near the end man.
Tight to the weak side, off the ball near the end man.
Widest man on the weak side.

aliases.term: Uno / Dos / Tres and A / B / C

motions.means: Lines up in the formation and goes across to the side called.
motions.onFilm: A man crosses the formation and is still moving or resets inside the far receiver.

motions.means: Across the formation all the way to an outside alignment.
motions.onFilm: Crosses and ends up as the widest or slot man on the far side.

motions.means: Short motion in toward the core without crossing the ball.
motions.onFilm: A receiver slides a few yards toward the tackle before the snap, often to block.

motions.means: Short motion that keeps going until he is inside the next receiver.
motions.onFilm: Outside receiver ends up inside the slot.

motions.means: Starts across, gets to about the guard, turns and goes back where he came from.
Starts on the wrong side and motions INTO the formation that was called. The call names the finish.
motions.onFilm: The picture at the snap is the formation. The start is a different look.

motions.means: Full speed jet motion: in front of the quarterback in the gun, behind him at about 3 yards under center.
motions.onFilm: Receiver at a sprint across the ball as it is snapped.

aliases.term: Fly (toward the play) / Flow (away from it)

motions.means: Motion across that goes behind the quarterback.
motions.onFilm: In the gun, a receiver runs behind the quarterback and back.

motions.means: The back changes sides on his own. No tag needed.
motions.onFilm: Fullback slides strong to weak, or the gun back hops to the other side of the quarterback.

motions.means: Halfback motions out of the backfield past the widest receiver: Hay to the Y's side, Hax to the X's side. Foy and Fox are the same for the fullback.
motions.onFilm: Back leaves the backfield and the set becomes empty.

motions.means: Motions into the backfield to the I spot.
motions.onFilm: A receiver or tight end ends up as a second back.

motions.means: Fly motion that goes AWAY from where the ball is going.
motions.onFilm: Jet motion one way, run or throw the other way.
Starts like a jet, pulls up.

motions.means: Fly motion across, then back to where he started.
motions.onFilm: Jet out and return before the snap.

motions.means: Across the ball, settles in an offset spot, then goes behind the quarterback in the gun.
motions.onFilm: Receiver loops behind the quarterback at the snap.

motions.means: Soar: two fly motions in a row. Counter Fly: across, then fly back. Flight: fly with a late snap.
motions.onFilm: A jet motion with an extra piece before it or a late snap.

motions.means: Jump: back starts in the pistol and steps to the gun spot. Skip: back in the offset gun moves on his own side. Hover: full speed behind the quarterback in the gun.
motions.onFilm: The back moves just before the snap without leaving the backfield.

motions.means: Dot: starts in the pistol spot behind the quarterback and motions out to the formation. Oz: Y starts outside the widest receiver away from the call and motions across into it.
motions.onFilm: A receiver or tight end starts somewhere odd and ends in the called formation.

motions.means: Run-game motion rules for blocking the force safety. Insert: short motion and fit inside. Maybe: he decides between inserting, crossing to the slot, or staying.
motions.onFilm: A receiver motions tight and blocks a safety.

shifts.means: The halfback starts as the widest receiver in an empty look, Lab on the left and Rat on the right, then shifts back into the backfield. Call it Lab to (formation).
shifts.onFilm: Opens in empty, back trots in, everybody resets.

aliases.term: Lab / Rat. Rope and Lasso add the Y coming across to a bunch

shifts.means: Starts in I Rt Ace. The Y shifts across, then the X motions across to finish in I Lt Hip.
shifts.onFilm: Tight end trades sides, then a receiver follows.

lineWords.means: Audible: the quarterback is changing the play. The new run or protection follows. Always on Turbo.
Flip the play to the other side out of a balanced formation. Alerted in the huddle: 18 alert Oscar becomes 19.
Two plays called in the huddle. Run the first unless the quarterback says Can, then run the second.
Cancels a Can or an Oscar: back to the first play.
The no-huddle package, and the fast cadence that goes with it.

chartRules.title: Strength is the Y
chartRules.means: The chart's Str column is the passing strength on 3x1. A call goes to the tight end. A tight end alone left with three receivers right is charted 3x1 Rt and called Fast Lt. PlayForge keeps both.

chartRules.title: A tag explains every difference
chartRules.means: A formation word puts every job in a spot. When film shows something else, a tag says why: Off (the Y backs off the ball and the Z steps on), Clamp (Y off, Z down to 5 yards on the ball), Click (Z on the ball inside, Y outside and off), Close and Closer (the Z comes in), Open and Out (the Y flexes), Tight and Tighter (the X comes in), Slot, Zoom, Hip, Hop. On import PlayForge builds every formation with every tag and keeps the call whose picture is the one on film. If nothing builds it, the formation is named from the picture and its note says so.

chartRules.title: Name the picture, list the twins
chartRules.means: Trips, Trio and Trax are one picture on film. So are Dice and Dixie, Stack and South, Bunch and Box. PlayForge names the first and lists the rest as same picture, different jobs. When I know who the F is that week, I can pick the exact word.

chartRules.title: A flexed tight end changes the word
chartRules.means: Tight end standing up 2 to 5 yards off the tackle is Open. In 2x2 that is Dyno, in 3x1 it is Trips Open, in 1x3 it is Fast Open.

chartRules.title: Empty
chartRules.means: Find the back among the five receivers, name the other four, add his letter.

chartRules.title: Closest word
chartRules.means: When a picture fits no book definition the nearest word is used and the formation is flagged closest word, check it.

chartRules.title: Same word, different picture
chartRules.means: Alignments are read off the Rams 2022 drawings (clean vector diagrams), named with the system word. Careful: a few words mean different pictures in the two books. Rams Open is the system's Out, Rams Tout is the system's Open, Rams Clout is the system's Click, Rams Trio is the system's Trout, Rams Trick is the system's Trio, Rams Box is the system's Bin, Rams Fast is the system's Foot. Two Rams pictures are left out because their word is already taken: Rams Trout (same picture on film as Trips Open) and Rams Buddy (same picture as Buddy). Rams-only words are kept as they are: Troff, Trey, Treat, Bundle, Bowl, the Jinx family (F alone away from a three-receiver side), Swift, Scoot, Fleet, King, Edge, Acer. On the Formations page, searching a Rams word (Double, Tout, Speed) finds the system formation.

workflow.means: The day-after routine. Claude does the pre-snap charting from the downloaded All-22 while I do something else, then I check its work and spend my own time on what the play was. About 20 minutes of waiting, then 90 minutes of my time for a 55 to 75 snap game.

passes.title: Set up
passes.question: Is everything ready for Claude?
steps: Download the All-22 from NFL Pro (Game Center, both angles in one file). Save it with the footage.

Run the all22-film-charting skill in Chrome for the TEXT pass only: Play ID, quarter, down and distance, yard line, play text, and personnel from the On Field Players list. Personnel from the list is the one thing video cannot give reliably.
Paste those rows into the workbook so the week has its Play IDs (W3-001 ...).
Tell Claude: chart week N from this file. Give it the video path.

passes.title: Pre-snap pass: Claude charts every snap
passes.question: What did they line up in?
steps: Claude splits the video into plays, matches each Eagles snap to its workbook row by yard line and order, and pulls the set frame from both angles.
It charts family, strength, backfield, hash, every eligible's alignment, and the motion note, with the set taken BEFORE any motion and AFTER any shift.
It compares its read with the workbook row and lists every disagreement with the reason.
Each snap gets a confidence for personnel / formation / hash. Names it cannot read stay unknown.

passes.title: Check and import
passes.question: Do I trust it?
steps: Read Claude's disagreement list first. Open those snaps in Film Lab and decide. Most are set-versus-motion calls: the system charts the set.
Spot check five other snaps at random, plus every snap rated M on formation.
Things video reads badly: on or off the ball, stack versus a tight pair, bunch versus tight trips, and receiver names. Fix what matters.
Claude runs the import. Every formation comes in with its system call: Gun Dice Rt, West Lt Slot, Gun Trips Lt G.
Twins (Trips / Trio / Trax, Dice / Dixie, Stack / South): leave the first word unless I know who the F was.
Write down which formations are new this week and which got the most snaps.

passes.title: Post-snap pass: name the play
passes.question: What did they run?
steps: Watch the end zone angle first for the line, then the sideline angle for routes.

Run: read the line's first two steps. Flat and wide = wide zone (18 / 19). Tighter, downhill = mid or tight zone (16 / 17, 14 / 15). Double teams and a puller = gap (12 / 13). Even number goes right, odd goes left. In the gun the first digit is 3.
Then the tag: who came across (Sift), who led, toss or handoff, fly motion with it. Look the word up in Run game.
Pass: first the type. Quick, dropback, play pass (name the run it copies), movement (Keep), or screen.
Then the protection (which way the line slides, where the back checks), then the concept by the strong-side routes, then the backside tag.
Write the whole call in order: shift, backfield, formation, variation, motion, number or protection, concept. Example: Gun Trips Rt F Fly 18 Zap.
Not sure of the word: write what I saw in plain words and mark it needs review. A plain description beats a wrong word.

passes.title: Diagram
passes.question: What goes in the book?
steps: Do not draw all 65. Draw each NEW play once, plus the three or four that mattered most.
Open the formation, start a play from it. The alignment is already right.
Add the motion first (dashed start spot), then blocks or routes, then number the quarterback's read.
Name the play with the call. In the notes: Play IDs it showed up on, down and distance, the defense's front and coverage, result.
A play they ran before: add this week's Play ID to the existing drawing instead of drawing it again.
Put the week's plays in one playbook for the season, a section per week.

passes.title: Wrap up
passes.question: What did I learn?
steps: Read This season so far at the bottom of this page: which formation words and motions went up or down.
Three lines in my notes: what was new, what they leaned on, what I expect next week.
Any word I had to invent or could not find: add it to my list to settle before next week so the language stays the same.
Print the week's sheet from the playbook if I want it on paper.

rules: One question per pass. Formation first, play second, drawing last.
Same words every week. If the system has a word, use it. If it does not, describe it and flag it.
The chart is facts from film. The drawing is my read. Keep them apart.
